name: Okavango Delta
description: In north-west Botswana, the Okavango River fans out across the Kalahari Desert instead of reaching the sea, spreading roughly 11 cubic kilometres of water over islands, channels and floodplains each year. The flood arrives in the dry season, drawing wildlife to its lush wetlands, including lions, cheetahs, wild dogs and both kinds of rhino. In 2014 it became the 1,000th site on the World Heritage List.
